title: Fine saturated nodal pushout monoid and its monoid-algebra model
statement: Let $P$ be a fine saturated commutative monoid, with group completion and fineness/saturation as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, and let $a\in P$. Put $R=\mathbf Z\oplus P$. Let $Q=\mathbf N^2\amalg_{\mathbf N}R$ be the pushout of commutative monoids for the maps $1\mapsto(1,1)$ and $1\mapsto(1,a)$; explicitly $Q$ is the quotient of $\mathbf N^2\oplus R$ by the congruence generated by $((1,1),0)\sim(0,(1,a))$. Then $Q$ is fine saturated, and the canonical map $g:R\to Q$ induces an injection $g^{\rm gp}:R^{\rm gp}\to Q^{\rm gp}$ with cokernel isomorphic to $\mathbf Z$. For every commutative ring $A$, multiplicative monoid map $\alpha:P\to(A,\cdot)$ and unit $\varepsilon\in A^\times$, give $A$ its $\mathbf Z[R]$-algebra structure by $(n,p)\mapsto\varepsilon^n\alpha(p)$. There is a canonical isomorphism of $A$-algebras $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[Q]\cong A[u,v]/(uv-\varepsilon\alpha(a))$, taking the two generators from $\mathbf N^2$ to $u,v$ and the elements of $R$ to the specified units and base monomials. Here $\mathbf Z[S]$ denotes the commutative monoid ring: the free abelian group on symbols $[s]$ with multiplication $[s][t]=[s+t]$.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9 proof, printed p. 71: cocartesian monoid square defining Q, cartesian monoid-ring square, and injectivity/cokernel calculation for g.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-pushout-coordinate-normal-form] to $P,a$; its integrality hypothesis follows from [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Obtain the injective $h:Q\to H$ with image $b-m_-a\in P$ and the isomorphism $h^{\rm gp}:Q^{\rm gp}\simeq H$, with the specified generator coordinates. Thus $Q\to Q^{\rm gp}$ is injective.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9 proof, printed p. 71: cocartesian monoid square defining Q, cartesian monoid-ring square, and injectivity/cokernel calculation for g.

proof.text: The monoid $Q$ is generated by $u,v,e,-e$ and the images of a finite generating set of $P$. If $r(m,t,b)\in h(Q)$ for an integer $r>0$, the image criterion of [lem-trf-nodal-pushout-coordinate-normal-form] gives $rb-(rm)_-a=r(b-m_-a)\in P$, since $(rm)_-=rm_-$. Saturation of $P$ gives $b-m_-a\in P$, hence $(m,t,b)\in h(Q)$. Together with step 1 these are precisely the three fine saturated conditions of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9 proof, printed p. 71: cocartesian monoid square defining Q, cartesian monoid-ring square, and injectivity/cokernel calculation for g.

proof.text: Under [lem-trf-nodal-pushout-coordinate-normal-form], $g^{\rm gp}(n,b)=(0,n,b)$, which is injective. Projection $(m,t,b)\mapsto m$ induces $Q^{\rm gp}/g^{\rm gp}(R^{\rm gp})\simeq\mathbf Z$: its inverse sends $m$ to the class of $(m,0,0)$; subtracting $(0,t,b)$ verifies both inverse identities. No sharpness or torsion-freeness of $P$ has been used.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9 proof, printed p. 71: cocartesian monoid square defining Q, cartesian monoid-ring square, and injectivity/cokernel calculation for g.

proof.text: For the algebra clause put $\beta(n,p)=\varepsilon^n\alpha(p)$ and $b_0=(1,a)\in R$. The unit hypothesis on $\varepsilon$ makes $\beta$ a monoid homomorphism for all $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $\beta(b_0)=c=\varepsilon\alpha(a)$. Set $D=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[Q]$ and $B=A[U,V]/(UV-c)$. Apply [lem-trf-binomial-monoid-tensor-universal-property] with $b=b_0$, $C=B$, $x=\bar U$, $y=\bar V$. It gives an $A$-algebra map $F:D\to B$ with $F(\lambda\otimes[(i,j,n,p)])=\lambda\bar U^i\bar V^j\varepsilon^n\alpha(p)$.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9 proof, printed p. 71: cocartesian monoid square defining Q, cartesian monoid-ring square, and injectivity/cokernel calculation for g.

proof.text: [lem-trf-binomial-monoid-tensor-universal-property] gives $U_DV_D=c\otimes[0]$ and $1\otimes[g(n,p)]=\varepsilon^n\alpha(p)\otimes[0]$. Polynomial evaluation [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] at $U_D,V_D$ sends every multiple $f(U,V)(UV-c)$ to $f(U_D,V_D)(U_DV_D-c)=0$. It is therefore constant on cosets of $(UV-c)$ and defines an $A$-algebra map $G:B\to D$. The composite $FG$ fixes $A,\bar U,\bar V$, hence every polynomial class by that universal property; $GF$ fixes $U_D,V_D$, hence is the identity by the cited uniqueness for maps out of $D$. Thus $F,G$ are inverse with the required branch and base-monomial images. These images determine $F$ uniquely, giving canonicity.
